title: UTC-aligned quota windows and invoice-friendly attribution for embeddings + rerank toolchains
creator: Marcus Liu
description:
Problem: composite non-chat requests (embeddings -> rerank -> optional toolcalls/structured output) are being metered across inconsistent windows and intermediate retries. This causes three issues: 1) customer-facing invoices split across UTC boundaries unpredictably; 2) double/partial charges when speculative prefetches or retries occur; 3) rate limit windows that don't align with billing windows lead to surprising quota exhaustion for customers in non-UTC timezones.

Goal: introduce a deterministic, UTC-aligned billing window and an invoice-friendly attribution model for composite embedding/rerank/toolcall requests. Make per-request provenance explicit so that multi-stage flows can be atomically checkpointed and prorated in a way that is reversible for refunds and audit. Ensure rate limits and quotas remain smooth (no sharp cliffs) while preserving per-window accounting for billing and customer reporting.
acceptance_criteria:
1) All embedding/rerank non-chat composite requests have a propagated usage_trace_id and are emitted as a single logical billing_event that references per-stage token counts.
2) Billing events are attributed to a UTC-aligned calendar window with deterministic proration when a request spans two windows.
3) Rate limits enforce fair-share using window alignment + leaky-bucket smoothing so customers do not experience sudden exhaustion at UTC boundary.
4) Dashboard and invoices reflect combined logical cost per logical request (no duplicate charges for speculative prefetches).
5) End-to-end tests for partial failures, retries, and cancellations demonstrating correct refunds/prorations.
implementation_notes:
High-level changes: 1) Add usage_trace_id header and wirethrough to all internal fncall/emitter codepaths. 2) Emit a single billing_event per logical request (billing_event contains per-stage token breakdown). 3) Introduce billing_window_start (UTC midnight) into billing pipeline; compute deterministic prorate for tokens crossing windows using token timestamp order. 4) Rate limiter: replace strict rolling-window enforcement at quota boundary with small leaky-bucket layer plus fixed-window counters for billing alignment. 5) DB: billing_events table add columns (usage_trace_id, logical_request_id, prorated_amount, window_start). Migration: backfill for last 7 days for analytics only, do not change past invoices.

Backward compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged unless customer opts into invoice-friendly attribution via org-level config. This avoids sudden billing model changes for existing customers while allowing enterprise customers (and trials) to opt in.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (flagged): server-side feature flag for usage_trace_id emission + billing_event aggregation (internal testing).
Phase 1: opt-in enterprise customers + dedicated test orgs; run dual-writing mode (old single-stage events + new aggregated logical billing events) for 2 weeks and reconcile.
Phase 2: enable UTC-window proration in billing pipeline for opted-in orgs; monitor refunds and reconciliation metrics.
Phase 3: public rollout with an opt-out grace period and customer communication plan.
Instrumentation: add metrics: billing_event_discrepancy_rate, prorate_error_rate, invoice_delta_median, rate_limit_boundary_spike.
Upgrade notes: console will include a toggle under Billing > Advanced to enable invoice-friendly attribution and link to migration FAQ.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Deterministic proration edge cases when stage ordering is nondeterministic (parallel fanout). Mitigation: enforce canonical ordering by token timestamp and stage index, break ties using stable hashing of usage_trace_id.
Risk: Customers on legacy billing may see different monthly totals when they opt-in. Mitigation: run dual-write and provide a reconciliation window + preview invoices for first month.
Risk: Increased complexity in billing pipeline causing latency. Mitigation: do heavy aggregation asynchronously; billing_event insert remains fast path with reference to intermediate S3/queue for full breakdown.
Risk: Rate limiter changes could affect perceived fairness. Mitigation: keep per-org steady-state rate cap identical; only smooth at sub-minute scales using leaky-bucket parameters validated by load tests.
